key_insight: FSW joint performance is governed by strong interactions among rotational speed, travel speed, and axial force, not by any single parameter alone.
engineering_relevance: For AA6061-T6 butt joints, tuning the process window can substantially improve strength and efficiency, with the best tested condition reaching an estimated 280.39 MPa UTS and 90.45% joint efficiency.
method: 3 × 3 × 3 full factorial design on rotational speed, travel speed, and axial force
81 mechanical-test observations with reported replicates across 27 parameter combinations
ANOVA and coded quadratic regression used to rank main effects and interactions
evidence_signal: All three parameters were significant for the four mechanical responses (p < .001), and the regression models explained 72.1%–84.6% of response variance.
watch_item: The recommended settings are model-based and should be applied cautiously outside the tested tool, material, and parameter ranges.
paper_title: Optimization of Friction Stir Welding Parameters for Improving the Mechanical Properties of Aluminum Alloy Joints
